title: A cheap stock SSD made my 128GB Strix Halo mini PC feel like a 2010 laptop
summary: Task Manager showed plenty of free CPU and RAM, while the SSD's shrinking cache quietly stalled every write.
content: My multi-thousand-dollar Strix Halo mini PC felt slower than a cheap Core 3 laptop after just a few weeks. I tried everything to figure out why this beast of a desktop was so laggy. It wasn’t the RAM, CPU, or anything else, so what could it be?

title: After 15 years on Ubuntu Server, Debian 13 might finally win me over
summary: Rust sudo and coreutils aren't battle-tested yet, and Debian never made the switch.
content: If you’re like me, then you probably reach for Ubuntu as a default server distro out of habit. I’ve done that for nearly 15 years. The problem is, Ubuntu isn’t what it used to be, and Debian is. Starting with Ubuntu 25.10, Canonical began the migration from using GNU’s core utilities to all-new Rust-based coreutils .

title: 4 DeWALT tools worth buying before winter rolls in
summary: Perfect for snowfall and cold nights.
content: It's that time of year again. The cold winter months are here, and you need to be prepared by getting out your winter tools or buying a few new ones. DeWALT makes all sorts of tools, and while you probably have some drills and drivers, did you know it also makes snowblowers, heated jackets, car jump starters, and more?

title: Docker containers are supposed to be lightweight, so why is my server running out of RAM?
summary: That innocent-looking Docker Compose file might be why your server is gasping for memory!
content: Docker containers are lightweight because they share the host operating system’s kernel, eliminating much of the overhead associated with running virtual machines. However, the applications inside those containers still have essentially the same memory requirements as they would if you installed them directly on your server.

title: Google Home's latest update brings 19 changes, including performance upgrades
summary: Bug fixes, performance improvements, and a handful of new features.
content: Google has released an update for the Google Home app and for Gemini for Home users in early access . The new patch delivers a "substantial" improvement in performance, fixes bugs with video playback, adds remote siren controls, and more. Google has either already added or begun rolling these features out. The process will take a few weeks, so you may or may not already have access to several features.

title: 3 Home Assistant projects to make your smart home safer this weekend (Nov 27-29)
content: AI can do a lot of amazing things, but not all of them are good for your smart home. Vibe-coded integrations can have security issues, and AI tools can make it easier to find vulnerabilities in smart homes and smart home devices that are exposed to the internet.

title: I bought a VR headset for productivity, not games
summary: I'm looking to make this my next PC
content: Galaxy XR is the most expensive computer I’ve ever purchased, but it felt justifiable—not as a gaming machine, but for work. I wanted this headset not just because I write about Android, but because it’s the kind of workspace I can easily see myself writing in.

title: I built my kids their own internet that doesn't need the internet
summary: It's a small World Wide Web after all.
content: The internet is an incredible source of information. If there's something you want to know, you'll probably be able to find it somewhere online. The problem is that there's a lot more than just useful information to be found online.

title: Make these 4 changes before charging your Galaxy Watch overnight
summary: Charge your watch more safely and quietly at night.
content: Many Galaxy Watch models can now last more than a day on a charge, but that might not fit into your routine. If you’re like me, you charge your phone overnight — it just makes sense to charge your watch, too. Here are a few tips to do it safely (and quietly).

title: Mini PCs still can't replace the Raspberry Pi's best feature
summary: Every way to add GPIO to a mini PC ends up adding a microcontroller.
content: Raspberry Pis used to be all about affordability, and now a Pi can cost the same as a mini PC . So, why should you still buy a Pi? Well, it has unique features that mini PCs still can’t fully replicate.
